alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued November 19 at 2:51AM EST until November 19 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Miami FL
alerts.description:
Bands of scattered showers and storms, on the north side of
developing low pressure, are expected to move inland across south
Florida today. The highest probability of being impacted by heavy
rain will be across Broward and Palm Beach counties today.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The metros of Miami-Dade and especially Broward and Palm
Beach counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread 3 to 5 inches of rain have fallen across the east
coast of South Florida over the past several days, with pockets
of 8 to 15 inches. Areas having received these higher end amounts
are most susceptible to today's forecast rain amounts.

100 AM EST Thu Nov 19 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Offshore the Southeast U.S. Coast:
A non-tropical low pressure system is expected to form near the 
northern Bahamas by late Friday.  This system could become a 
subtropical or tropical storm while it moves northward or 
northeastward near or just offshore of the southeastern U.S. coast 
through the weekend.  Regardless of development, strong winds, 
dangerous surf, and coastal flooding are likely along portions of 
the southeast and mid-Atlantic coasts into early next week.  
Interests along the eastern U.S. coast should monitor the progress 
of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.
